status: First adult-use retail market in the United States (sales from January 2014). Regulator: Marijuana Enforcement Division (MED) within the Department of Revenue. Sales and tax data are published as open datasets on data.colorado.gov and refreshed monthly.

facts.label: Decline in annual sales from the 2021 peak to 2025
facts.source: Colorado Department of Revenue, Marijuana Sales Revenue in Colorado (Socrata dataset p6y8-s74x), monthly rows summed by calendar year
facts.verify: Annual totals of total_marijuana_sales: 2021 $2,228,994,553 (peak), 2022 $1,768.7M, 2023 $1,529.3M, 2024 $1,397.1M, 2025 $1,315,678,364. 2025 is 41.0% below 2021. Dataset covers 2014-01 through 2026-04 at retrieval; 2026 is partial and must never be presented as a full year.

facts.label: January to April 2026 sales, the sixth consecutive decline in that window
facts.source: Same CDOR sales revenue dataset, months 1-4 summed per year
facts.verify: January-April totals: 2021 $768.1M, 2022 $611.9M, 2023 $525.4M, 2024 $476.6M, 2025 $436.8M, 2026 $416.6M. Like-for-like four-month windows, which is the only honest way to use the partial 2026 data. 2026 is 45.8% below the same window in 2021.

facts.label: Statewide sales in May 2026, the latest month with county detail
facts.source: Colorado Department of Revenue, Marijuana Sales by County in Colorado (Socrata dataset j7a3-jgd3)
facts.verify: 'Total' row for 2026-05: medical $9,046,036 plus retail $98,485,414 = $107,531,450. The 46 individual county rows sum to $106,326,709, $1.2M short of the Total row, because some counties are suppressed or marked NR. Use the Total row as the denominator for any share calculation and say so.

facts.label: Denver County's share of statewide sales, May 2026
facts.verify: Denver $25,354,541 of the $107,531,450 Total row = 23.6%. Next largest: El Paso $11,696,079, Arapahoe $11,303,004, Adams $9,070,823, Larimer $8,003,242. Those five are 60.8% of the state. Seven of 46 county rows report zero.

facts.label: Medical sales in 2025, down from a 2016 peak of $445.6 million
facts.source: Same CDOR sales revenue dataset, total_medical_marijuana_sales summed by year

facts.label: Cumulative marijuana taxes and fees collected since 2014
facts.source: Colorado Department of Revenue, Marijuana Tax and Fee Revenue (Socrata dataset 3sm5-jtur), total_taxes_fees summed
facts.verify: 149 monthly rows from 2014-02 through 2026-06 sum to $3,223,897,183. Recent years: 2023 $274.1M, 2024 $255.4M, 2025 $236.4M. Note this dataset runs one to two months ahead of the sales datasets; never pair a tax month with a sales month without checking both.

facts.label: Licensed marijuana facilities in Denver
facts.source: City and County of Denver open data, BUSN_MARIJUANAFACILITIES_P feature layer
facts.verify: 254 records, layer lastEditDate 2026-08-24. By license name: Marijuana Store 247, Marijuana Hospitality 7. By type: Retail 166, Medical 81, Mobile Hospitality 3, Hospitality with Sales 3, Hospitality 1. By status: License Issued - Active 250, Awaiting Customer Inspections 3, Delinquent 1. This is a city licence count and is not comparable to a state MED store count.

facts.label: Denver County's share of Colorado sales in 2025, down from 47.7% in 2014
facts.source: Colorado Department of Revenue, Marijuana Sales by County (j7a3-jgd3), Denver rows and Total rows summed by calendar year within the same dataset
facts.verify: Share by year: 2014 47.7, 2015 40.9, 2016 38.4, 2017 38.3, 2018 34.7, 2019 33.2, 2020 32.4, 2021 30.6, 2022 26.9, 2023 26.1, 2024 25.5, 2025 23.9, 2026 partial 23.5. Twelve consecutive annual declines. Both numerator and denominator come from the same dataset, so the share is internally consistent; do not compute it against the separate statewide revenue dataset, which has a different latest month.

facts.label: Denver County sales in 2025, down 55.6% from the 2020 peak
facts.source: Same CDOR county sales dataset, Denver rows summed by year
facts.verify: Denver annual: 2014 $325.9M, 2017 $577.5M, 2020 $709.5M (peak), 2021 $682.1M, 2022 $475.5M, 2023 $399.0M, 2024 $356.4M, 2025 $314,810,969. Peak-to-2025 is -55.6%; 2021-to-2025 is -53.8% against the state's -41.0% over the same span, which is why Denver's share fell. 2026 county data covers January to May only.

gaps: Statewide store count: the MED licensed-facilities file sits behind a CloudFront block that refuses both curl and a headless browser (sbg.colorado.gov returns 403 / 'request could not be satisfied'). Do not state how many dispensaries Colorado has. Denver's own city layer is usable and is the only licence count on file.
Reasons for the sales decline: not published by any state source. The datasets show the trend and nothing about its causes. Never assert a cause on a page.

The three CDOR datasets have different currency (sales revenue through 2026-04, county sales through 2026-05, tax through 2026-06). Never pair figures across them without checking each one's latest period.
2026 is a partial year in every dataset. Only like-for-like windows (January to April) may be compared to prior years.
County rows do not sum to the published Total row (a $1.2M gap in May 2026) because small counties are suppressed or marked NR. Share calculations must use the Total row and disclose the gap.
